standard_prerequisites: Context span 2935-2941: definition of the fixed field K^G

Same chapter: lemma-finite-Galois (finite extension Galois iff |Aut(E/F)| = [E:F], stated and proved at source lines 2880-2894), lemma-recognize-separable (a divisor of a separable polynomial is separable), lemma-primitive-element (finite separable extensions are simple), lemma-normal-and-automorphisms (the automorphism bound inequality)
core_obligations: For alpha in K the orbit polynomial P = prod over beta in G.alpha of (x - beta) is G-invariant, hence lies in K^G[x], and has alpha as a root; so K/K^G is algebraic, and the minimal polynomial Q of alpha divides P, so Q is separable and K/K^G is separable, hence Galois

Faithfulness gives finitely many alpha_i whose common fixed set in G is trivial; setting L = K^G({sigma(alpha_i)}) the degree [L : K^G] equals |G|, and L = K, since adjoining any element outside L without enlarging L is absurd

In the finite case K = K^G(alpha) by the primitive element lemma; the orbit construction gives deg(alpha) <= |G|, and faithfulness of the G-action on L plus the automorphism bound gives deg(alpha) >= |G|; hence [K : K^G] = |G| and the Galois group is G by lemma-finite-Galois
proof_roadmap: Prove K/K^G algebraic, separable and Galois via the invariant orbit polynomial
Reduce to the finite case through the separating tuple alpha_i and the subfield L
Conclude the degree equality from the two-sided orbit bound
